_readme: The corpus source list, FIXED BEFORE ANYTHING WAS FETCHED.
Why a fixed list matters here even though the content does not: the experiment measures
whether a training run reproduces bit for bit, not what the model learns. Corpus content is
irrelevant to every one of the seven measurements. What the corpus MUST be is licence-clean
and redistributable, because a corpus we cannot redistribute makes the replication package
impossible -- and the replication package is the thing the paper is about.
So the selection rule is not about quality or representativeness. It is:
1. published before 1929 and in the public domain in the United States
2. available from Project Gutenberg as a plain-text file
3. English prose or drama, so a single tokenizer is defensible
4. fixed in this file, with digests recorded on first fetch, before the Merkle root is
committed and before the first training step
Project Gutenberg's licence attaches to its TRADEMARK and its boilerplate, not to the
public-domain works themselves. build_corpus.py strips everything outside the START/END
markers, so the corpus carries no PG branding and no PG licence obligation. This is the
arrangement PG's own terms describe for public-domain texts with the trademark removed.
raw_sha256 is filled by fetch_corpus.py on first retrieval and never edited afterwards. A
changed upstream file is a FINDING -- Project Gutenberg does revise its texts -- and it is
selection_rule: pre-1929 US public domain, plain text from Project Gutenberg, English, boilerplate stripped; content is irrelevant to the measurements and the list is fixed before fetching so it cannot be tuned
